properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. The most concrete of the Class B candidates in `dec:idea-which-agent-pitfalls-can-reflow2-actually-reach`, separated because it is a specific buildable proposal rather than a triage, and because its measured bound is the interesting part.

THE PITFALL, in Anthony's words 2026-08-17: "Infinite loops: Agents can get stuck repeatedly adding and removing the exact same line of code to fix a recurring error."

THE IDEA. reflow2 does not read code, but it records CONTENT HASHES. An oscillation has a signature that needs no semantic understanding at all: an artifact's checksum returning to a value it already held. A → B → A is a loop, and A → B → C → B is a smaller one. No language server, no diff parsing, no judgement — just a repeat in a sequence.

⭐ THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE FOR REFLOW2 SPECIFICALLY, which is why it is worth separating out. Everything else in the pitfall list needs to understand code; this needs only to notice that the design has seen this exact content before. It is the same move `orphan_node`'s degree-zero rule makes — the finding that needs no judgement is the one worth computing.

⚠️⚠️ AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS IT CANNOT BE BUILT TODAY, which is the part that would have been missed by proposing it on plausibility. MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH, 2026-08-17:
    Artifacts with ANY snapshotted checksum history:      23   (of 187 artifacts)
    ...with more than one recorded prior value:             3
    ...showing a checksum that returns to a prior value:    0
The three deepest histories (`art:heal`, `art:detect`, `art:service`) hold TWO prior checksums each. A detector run on that data would report zero oscillations and mean nothing by it — the vacuous zero this whole epoch exists to stamp out, shipped inside the fix for it.

⇒ THE ROOT CAUSE IS ONE FIELD, NOT A SUBSYSTEM, and naming it is what makes this actionable. A Snapshot is taken by `record_change`, which the `design_updated` disposition calls and `design_holds` DOES NOT. So the commonest kind of code change — the refactor, the test fix, the churn where an oscillation would actually live — mints a ChangeEvent and records NO PRIOR CHECKSUM. The history is thin precisely where the signal would be.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(A) HAVE `design_holds` SNAPSHOT THE PRIOR CHECKSUM TOO. Smallest change; the history starts accumulating immediately; the detector becomes possible later without further work. COST: a Snapshot per accept, on the commonest path.
(B) KEEP A CHECKSUM LEDGER ON THE ARTIFACT rather than snapshotting the whole node — cheaper per write, but new vocabulary and a second place history lives.
(C) DON'T BUILD IT. Oscillation may be better caught by the agent harness, which sees the edits as they happen, than by a design graph seeing them after the fact.
(D) BUILD THE HISTORY NOW, THE DETECTOR LATER — deliberately, on the record, so the data exists by the time anyone wants the answer. This is the option the measurement argues for.

📌 THE GENERAL LESSON, worth keeping whatever is decided: the detector was easy and the DATA was the constraint, and that was invisible until it was counted. Proposing it on plausibility would have produced a check that reports zero forever and is believed.
properties.name: OPEN — an artifact whose checksum RETURNS to a previous value is an agent going in circles; the detector is trivial and the history reflow2 keeps is too thin to run it on
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. The detector is trivial — a repeat in a sequence of content hashes, needing no semantic understanding — and reflow2 cannot run it: only 23 of 187 artifacts have any snapshotted checksum history and only 3 have more than one prior value, because `design_holds` accepts do not snapshot. The root cause is one missing write on the commonest path, not a missing subsystem. Proposing this on plausibility would have shipped a check that reports zero forever.
